acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Retrieval agent defined with tool interface per AWS Strands agentic framework - Agent decorated with @tool decorator from AWS Strands - Agent signature follows Strands tool conventions - Agent registered with orchestrator as callable tool

Agent accepts query and returns relevant document chunks with citations - Input: Natural language query string, optional top_k parameter - Output: JSON-serialized list of DocumentChunk objects with metadata - Citations include page numbers, document IDs, scores, section types

Agent integrates with existing retrieval logic from Epic 1-2 - Wraps multi_index_search() from raglite.retrieval.multi_index_search - Leverages existing query classification logic (simple/table/analytical) - Reuses Epic 2 multi-index architecture (Qdrant + PostgreSQL) - No code duplication—direct function calls to existing modules

Agent tested in isolation (unit test) - Unit test validates agent interface and return format - Mocked multi_index_search() prevents external dependencies - Test execution time <100ms (framework overhead only) - Test validates JSON serialization of results

Agent tested within simple workflow (integration test) - Integration test executes Retrieval → Synthesis 2-agent workflow - Test uses real Qdrant instance (requires docker-compose up) - Test validates agent coordination via AWS Strands orchestrator - Test execution time <5s (includes real search latency)

constraints.constraint: KISS Principle: This is a ~50 line wrapper function. No abstractions, no custom base classes. Direct function calls only to multi_index_search().
Wrapper Pattern: Must wrap raglite.retrieval.multi_index_search directly. NO code duplication. Preserve Epic 2 query classification (simple/table/analytical).
AWS Strands @tool Decorator: Use @tool decorator from strands package. Function must be async and return JSON-serializable string (not Pydantic model directly).
Graceful Degradation (NFR24): If search fails → return empty results with error metadata. If timeout (>15s per NFR26) → return partial results. User always receives response.
Performance Target (NFR5): <3s p50, <8s p95 latency. Log execution time via AgentState.execution_time_ms for monitoring.
Test Isolation: Unit tests must mock multi_index_search() (no Qdrant dependency). Integration tests use real Qdrant but MockSynthesisAgent (no LLM API calls).
Structured Logging: Use logger.info() with extra={} for all agent executions. Include: query, top_k, execution_time_ms, success, results_count.
Type Hints Required: All function signatures must have type annotations. Follow existing codebase patterns from Story 3.1.

interface.name: retrieval_agent
interface.signature: @tool async def retrieval_agent(query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> str
interface.description: Retrieval Agent tool interface. Accepts natural language query, calls multi_index_search(), returns JSON-serialized DocumentChunk list with metadata.

interface.name: multi_index_search
interface.signature: async def multi_index_search(query: str, top_k: int = 5, search_mode: str = "auto") -> QueryResult
interface.description: Epic 2 multi-index search (90% accuracy). Returns QueryResult with chunks (List[DocumentChunk]), search_metadata (classification, backend used, latency). INTEGRATION POINT - wrap directly.

interface.name: AgentState
interface.description: State management model from Story 3.1. Fields: query, agent_type, success, result, execution_time_ms. Use validate_required_fields() before passing to orchestrator.

interface.name: create_orchestrator
interface.description: Orchestrator factory from Story 3.1. Add retrieval_agent to tools list here. Returns Strands Agent with MistralModel and system prompt.

interface.name: MockSynthesisAgent
interface.signature: @tool async def mock_synthesis_agent(analysis_results: str, original_query: str) -> str
interface.description: Mock synthesis agent from Story 3.1. Use in integration tests (Task 4) to avoid real LLM API calls. Returns hardcoded synthesis for testing.

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio for async support. Unit tests mock all external dependencies (multi_index_search, Qdrant, PostgreSQL). Integration tests use real Qdrant instance (docker-compose up -d required) but mock LLM calls (use MockSynthesisAgent). Test execution time targets: Unit tests <100ms each, Integration tests <5s each. Follow patterns from tests/unit/agentic/test_mock_agents.py and tests/integration/test_agentic_framework.py. Use pytest.mark.asyncio for async tests. Assert on execution time with pytest-timeout.
